target_customer: Construction developers, contractors and design-build firms in India
problem: Construction teams run site, procurement, design and finance in disconnected tools, causing delays and cost leakage.
business_model: B2B SaaS construction ERP, sister to 91Squarefeet design-and-build services

founders.name: Amit Bansal
education: Civil engineering degree; postgraduate degree in supply chain management

competitors.name: Powerplay
competitors.what: Construction management app for Indian contractors
competitors.funding_then: $5.2M from Accel and Sequoia's Surge, July 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrating site, procurement, design and finance modules with accounting and ERP tools is standard but broad enterprise software; AI features came later.

defensibility.rationale: ERP-style deployments are sticky once adopted, and the sister design-build business supplies workflow data, but several funded rivals exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying reported; company stayed independent with 80 staff per YC.

market_need_then: Indian construction projects rely on spreadsheets and chat; investors funded construction software in 2021 (Powerplay), showing demand.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is confusable with Redash (an unrelated BI tool) in search; little press on the brand.

outcome_analysis: RDash grew out of 91Squarefeet, a design-and-build firm run by the same founders who previously co-founded Quifers, a logistics SaaS company acquired in 2021. A $10M round led by Stellaris with Y Combinator was reported in September 2022 under the 91Squarefeet name, and the YC page now lists RDash at 80 people. Founder domain experience supported its growth; no failure signals were found.
notes: The $10M round is recorded as stage other: YourStory calls it a Series A for 91Squarefeet while Seedtable calls it seed for RDash; entity attribution is uncertain because 91Squarefeet and RDash are sister brands (legal entity Vonken Brandtech per directories). Amit Mishra is also named as a founder in coverage (YourStory/Silicon Review) but not on the YC page, so not listed. Total funding figures conflict ($5.6M across 8 rounds on TheCompanyCheck). Caplight page banner about a $16M Series A is unrelated. rdash.io fetch returned 503. Caplight lists a Jan 2022 pre-seed, unverified.
